Death Howl is a wonderfully dark and compelling experience that truly stands out. The game’s visual style is its biggest strength; the limited color palette and gritty pixel art create a unique and deeply atmospheric world that is instantly absorbing. The gameplay loop is challenging, mixing strategic choices with satisfying combat moments that feel rewarding after every victory. If you are looking for a game with a strong sense of atmosphere and rewarding difficulty, Death Howl delivers a powerful and memorable adventure.

I don't like it. You'll visit different worlds with each a flair and an associated set of cards ... its focus is very much the adventure rather than the strategy. Because of that restriction, the depth of the deckbuilding aspect is shallower than what one might expect : it's a tight environment of some cards already tailored to go together. Again, the focus isn't so much on the gameplay and deckbuilding aspect, but on the narrative. The player is put in a situation where they have to farm small scale fights of a region to acquire their ressources to craft their cards (as well as unlocking meta-progression specific to the said-region) in order to beat the Elites that guard the progression. You have maxHP but fights pose little strategic threat and you can revisit your save point to replenish HP when you feel like it. And that's a problem : forcing mindless farm of weightless fights and then resetting it all is a bad pace design. The problem is ... how robust is the story, the dialogues, the script and does it warrant you going through? I don't think it's compelling enough but it's better you judge for yourself if after a few hours you want to play it in full. So in the end, I don't know who this game is for. It seems to be 2 half-baked parts put together instead of one fully realised idea. One can make a walking-sim with good narrative, it's fine. One can forego narration entirely and make a godlike gameplay, it's fine too. But if you make a walking-sim and you ain't good at telling stories it's a bit of a problem. After a little less than 3 hours, I doubt I'll come back to it. You can go ahead and criticize me for criticizing this game but if all you have to say is "it's a small team so they are exempt of receiving a negative review" that's really stupid and not critical.

战棋+魂的创意不错，画风也很有意思。 但是战棋+魂+卡牌你是咋想的！！！！ 然后卡牌还得依靠资源区刷你又是咋想的！ 我玩魂是可以靠着反复学习和磨练，依靠操作和反应的。你卡牌的随机性是以为我的运气也可以通过反复重开提升吗？ 很多对局能不能过，完全是看发牌员心情。重开除了负面反馈，没有其他意义。 杠精可以说，那你可以调整卡牌构筑呀! 老子构筑你大爷！， 且不说每个地区的卡牌不一样，图腾不一样，天赋不一样， 你跨区域打牌 卡牌会有加费的debuff！ 也就是说，你以前好用的牌在这里由于加费不好用了，然后弄新牌你的刷资源打怪。甚至有些区域拍我得打这个区域的怪才能拿到， 我明明是打不过这个区域的怪才去刷新牌的呀！！！！！！！ 在这种情况下，很多怪物的攻击和技能还完谜语人！ 妥妥初见杀！ 你单反不是个抖m 你肯定不喜欢这个游戏！

纯粹卖美术创意噱头的游戏，我愿称之为爬塔和陷阵之志的不孝子，完美结合了二者的缺点再加上从类魂一脉相承的角色性能差距，然后硬是没从三者身上学到一点好的，对，是一点都没有。想打牌可以去爬塔火车，想玩硬核高难度战棋可以玩陷阵之志，想玩类魂更是一挑一大把何必浪费时间来吃这一坨？ 追加长评，欢迎理性讨论： 我觉得这游戏不管作为卡牌游戏或类魂或策略战棋的任意一种或多种复合都是很难达到平均水准的。 作为卡牌游戏来讲，就我目前刚进第二个区域的进度而言我真的没有看到什么深度和构筑性，如果后期会有的话我也不知道反正已经退款了。抛开这些不谈，游戏的几乎所有状态效果都没法查询也不像其他绝大部分游戏把鼠标放到高亮字体上有补充说明，完全只能靠猜或者头铁去试，敌人的强攻机制有0个说明基本全靠自己理解，恶心人的疯狗怪更是遍地走动不动就飞过来咬你一口大的，前期在位移和防御拉扯手段都很弱的时候面对复数威胁源基本是强制战损，如果被反击上心碎buff的怪蹭到这把基本上是交代了。我的体验是差不多打两架就要睡一觉然后重复这个循环，构筑卡组的资源基本上需要靠压战损堆出来，然而令人吊诡的是压战损的前提就是逐步构筑卡组，并且升级需要的泪滴数基本可以说是强制你去刷还跨区域不通用，我看这游戏改名叫死亡循环或者死亡刷子算了。 作为战棋游戏来讲我认为也是不合格的，首先缝合卡牌游戏使得运气因素被极大幅度的强化，爬过塔的朋友都知道就算你卡组bd已经完全成型可以原地开转也有可能第一回合鬼抽烂完吃大战损，而战棋和类魂，虽然对这游戏来讲类魂只是个噱头，但这两种游戏类型我认为都是极端的风险/运气厌恶型，都是基本纯粹靠磨练并提升相关的技术和能力推进游戏流程的，完全以成就感为正反馈的核心导向去设计的，而运气和成就感的联系程度就像死亡呼啸和类魂这个游戏类型的联系程度一样聊胜于无。抛开设计师这种令人诟病的，灵感大王式的，俺寻思之力一般的一拍脑袋就去做的游戏设计底层思路，转到表层来看它也是很难拿到及格分的。 首先叠甲，我玩过且深度玩的战棋游戏有且只有陷阵之志，以下是依据我对“战棋”这一游戏类别必定不完全正确，客观的游戏理解做出的批判，如果出现了逻辑/理解比较大的问题各位看个乐就行。 根据我的理解，战棋中最核心的两种资源是移动力和血量，两者很大程度上可以相互代偿和转化。而战棋游戏在很多时候会要求你在这两种资源中进行或显性或隐性的取舍，因而对设计者的数值平衡以及机制设计功底提出了很高的要求。基于这一点我们可以比较轻松的得出，在战棋游戏里设计类似于“反击”的机制是有待商榷的，因为这是近乎强制的血量资源损失，并且（在贴身反击情况下）强制你使用本应用于解决其他威胁源的远程攻击也会带来跨回合的隐性资源损失。且由于反击并不是临时性的buff，它具有永续性，所以用移动力和其他不对敌人造成伤害的操作代偿血量损失无异于饮鸠止渴，是没有任何可行性的。而注意我们上面说的仅限于贴身反击，而如果我没记错的话，这游戏有可以在4-5格的距离上*强力*反击你的怪，还密码的不是精英怪，就是随处可见的鳄鱼。在这个前提下“有待商榷”和“近乎强制”可以换成“完全不可接受”和“完全强制性”。对于贴脸反击挂虚弱/心碎的怪而言，期望上的战损相当于吃正常反击1.5刀或者强制少打一刀原地罚站，更别提还可以复合上述的远程反击还有沟槽的黄金搭档心碎+毒，被连到就是稳定的10+战损已经可以重开了。上述这些问题让本就不富裕的输出环境雪上加霜，我时常怀疑这游戏学的是不是搜打撤但是少学了前面两个字，让我的游戏体验不是在大地图跑三百六十五里路就是在战斗中跑路嘻嘻我一定要活下去。至少这个游戏在现在这个版本宛如一位躺在ICU行将就木的重症患者，也只能送上一句逝者为大了。 它并不是什么“开山之作”，缝合的2.5种游戏类型已经有现成的，数不胜数的良好设计思路，有参考性的数值平衡，有深度的游戏机制，还有无数的血泪教训和前车之鉴。虽然显得严苛但我觉得结合售价来看，它不应该是现在这样的完成度和质量，至少对我来讲这是不可接受的。这也是我不推荐它的核心原因，因为你并不是除了玩这游戏别无选择，玩这游戏的时间完全可以拿去玩点别的独立游戏。而且因为我昨天上午是满怀期待的打开这游戏然后捏着鼻子品鉴了四个小时所以你也可以认为我是在泄愤^^

It's alright. It's good in fact. But it's a refund from me. Death Howl tries to do two things at the same time, but it falls off a little short. It attempts to be narrative in its pacing and design, but the gameplay relying on you going geographically through A-B-C-D, then returning to A every time you reach C a few times to grind/get materials messes with the storytelling aspect. Since the encounters are custom designed and not randomly generated, that B and C points are the same every time, so it's not that fun to repeat them. The sound design was an amazing surprise. Really sells the spiritual journey. The colour scheme is gorgeous, but they kinda went overboard with the pixel art thing. Looks overblown and lacks detail on a screen larger than a deck's. Even though I agree pixels were the right choice, a little more detail could have lifted the feeling of staring at duplo building blocks. I like the cards and the combat is alright, but I think the navigation aspect of it could have been re-thought to house the narrative better.

Okay, I really wanted to like this one, as the art, and basic game idea seem great to me. However, this one not only gets a "no", it gets a "HELL NO" from me. There are some just flat-out terrible game design choices here. One of the early quests involves you picking up a bird, but when you do, enemies respawn behind you, blocking off your path, and you are penalized for having the bird. Having it in your hand will let an enemy respawn that turn (which is a life or death choice in many cases), or you can spend 3 points to discard the bird. The problem is, you only have 5 points early on, so that effectively ends your turn. With small maps, and enemies that can teleport, and shoot a projectile in one turn (basically covering the entire map), you are defenseless if you do that. The bird doesn't leave until you get through a few battles. You are not given the option to give up the quest, etc., effectively ending your run. Didn't see that coming as a player? F*ck you. Start your game over. This lack of options for navigating obstacles that can end your game is frankly unacceptable, particularly as you have no way of reading the future to know you will get trapped by your decisions.

I wanted to like this game, but the sheer lack of any real instruction on how to play the game makes it nigh unplayable. Sometimes you will go into a fight and only have 4 energy instead of 5. Why? This game needs a balance overhaul badly and a reworking of its progression system. It is one thing for a game to be hard, it is another thing for it to make me ram my head through the same encounters just to grind up enough to lose slightly less badly. Progression in this game is slow, unsatisfying, and it seems expect me to grind which I was hoping was a trend we left behind in the 90s. Grinding doesn't even make me feel any stronger in the game, it just gives me access to marginally better cards. I have the same amount of energy, the same amount of health, and the same hand size. I normally love deckbuilders but this one has me regretting my purchase. I should have played the demo first and then not waste my money on it. Sorry, the storyline can't keep me engaged through the game's painful mechanics, lack of meaningful progression, and unreasonable difficulty.

I played this for 3 hours, and had fun for a combined total of maybe 5 minutes. Look, I really like 11bitstudios, I played almost every game they published, I recommended all of them here, but this one, this is just suffering for the sake of it. This is as much fun as trying to fill taxes. I'm gonna try to be a bit nice and say that the visual style is decent (not good, decent, there are PLENTY of pixel art games that look way better than this one), and that the deck building has potential to be good. POTENTIAL. Let me use that to transition into the first HUGE problem this game has, as a deckbuilder, and it is an absolute dealbreaker for me. - Each combat is an area, divided like a chessboard by a grid. - You have 20 health points, I played 3 hours, as far as I know, there is no way to increase it - You'll be constantly outnumbered 1v3 or 1v4. EACH combat scenario is difficult. - So in almost every combat encounter, you'll lose a portion of those 20 HP. So your HP will drain pretty quickly. - How do you heal may you ask? Well the ONLY way to heal is to rest at a campfire. In soulslike fashion, it respawns ALL the enemies. So far, you'll just be tempted to call me out and say "git gud" and in a soulslike, you may be correct. Except for two things: - this is a deckbuilder and combat encounters are always the same, they are not randomized. You'll do 2/3 combat, need a healing, go and rest, this will reset everything, now to go back to a previous spot to clear the rest of the area you'll likely have to kill the SAME enemies again. mind you, each combat encounter is several minutes. this got old REALLY QUICKLY. - [b] but the WORST PART IS THIS: THE RESOURCE NEEDED TO HEAL AT CAMPFIRES, OBTAINED BY KILLING ENEMIES, IS THE SAME RESOURCE USED TO CRAFT NEW CARDS!!!!!!!!!! [/b] this is the dumbest game design decision I've ever seen in a game that takes itself seriously and doesn't present itself as some shovelware slop (and this game isn't that, it's clearly been crafted with care). so let me round that up for you: - you have limited HP, you'll lose some every fight - you can't heal except by resting at campfires and this will reset all enemies and use up ALL of your resource used to craft cards - [b] so you won't be able to craft any cards (IN A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ DECKBUILDER!!!). [/b] [b] effectively, in 3+ hours of gameplay I was able to craft a grand total of 3 cards. that is just ridiculous. [/b] it has the slowest and sluggiest progression I've ever seen in a videogame like this. my deck was virtually the same after clearing about 30 combat encounters, including fully clearing the entire first area, than at the very start of the game. this is just unacceptable in a game like this. after 3 hours I just realized the game wasnt going anywhere, the progression wasnt going anywhere, the story was non existant so far, I lost any willingness to keep playing. my suggestion, if devs read this, crafting new cards ALREADY requires loot from defeated monsters. you ALREADY must clear out a large portion of the map to craft new cards, and engage with your game. this is requirement enough, you do NOT need to ALSO require the SAME resource necessary for healing AND converting into skillpoints. so unfortunatly, there is no way I can recommend this. there is 0 progression (unless you mind-numbingly farm some easy camps over and over and over so you can slowly get the resource to craft the cards but I aint doin that ♥♥♥♥), its 2026, there are thousands of games on the market, the game needs to be engaging and draw the player in, and this kind of repetitive bs is well past its prime. I don't care about the difficulty, the game being hard/punishing/whatever, but if you prevent me from crafting new cards in your DECKBUILDER game, I won't be playing it.

I own this game, but my boyfriend has played it for 54.1 hours using Steam Family Library. He wrote a whole review before Steam told him he has to own the game in order to review it. So, here is his review, which I am under instructions to post. --- If you liked the second act of Inscryption you'll love this. People saying it's too hard are playing it wrong - I give up quickly and hate difficult games, but this was a perfect brain teaser and very satisfying to succeed at. People get confused by the soulslike label. It is a puzzle game disguised as a turn-based tactical RPG wrapped in a pure deckbuilder. The synergies are easy to find but tinkering with the deck to optimise it is very rewarding. The hunter-gatherer and explorer aspect are both enjoyable, the map is excellent and the progression is steady. The enemies are diverse. The art is goregous, I would absolutely buy a full hardcover artbook if I could. The world is filled with creepy, grizzly beauty and extremely unique landmarks. The story is wonderful. There is a not overwhelming but certainly not dry number of side quests, and the quality of them is very good. They range in difficulty and strategy and add a lot of flavour to the game. The only thing I would change at all is being able to see which caves I've completed - I ended up keeping a list myself. You can get a good amount of hours out of the game without being a completionist, and it took me 50 hours to do absolutely everything the game has to offer. I really enjoyed this game start to finish. --- I'm glad he's finished it because I was enjoying it and would like to play it as well :)

The idea of a +1 cost for cards in the other realm “letting” players experiment with different builds is incredible. Players are intelligent human beings. We don’t need you to tell us what to do. It limits flexibility and the fun of combining and experimenting with different ideas. Not to mention how awful the economy system is. The battle system is interesting. I highly doubt such a stubborn mindset deserves a positive review. Despite so many players complaining in the reviews about the +1 cost, your team insists it’s a good idea. And fk soulslike. Soulslike is the worst. Soulslike represents authority forcing people. Soulslike is pure disrespect for players’ time. You don’t even need to call yourself soulslike, because the most soulslike element in your game is the terrible economy system, causing a repetitive and torturous game experience. Card players use their brains instead of rote memorization and meaningless practice. How could a strategy game be soulslike?

There is alot to like about this game. The art style and atmosphere are amazing and the music is great too. But when it comes to the actual gameplay I don‘t like it at all. Coming from Slay the Spire I thought this was a no brainer. Turns out I was wrong. The game is not like StS at all but more like Magic The Gathering deckbuilding with grid-based movement where you can build multiple decks with different synergies beforehand. Nothing wrong with that but here‘s what ruined the game for me. Act I was really fun and also a bit challenging and a perfect introduction. After that, the game opens up and you unlock different regions to explore. Sounds good but the difficulty of the game is going from 1 to 10 really quick. Maybe I‘m just too dumb but it feels like you have to build a different deck for each encounter and I‘m not talking about Boss fights but regular fights too. And even then it feels way too dependant on RNG. Not saying the game is bad but it‘s just not my cup of tea.

I know everyone is playing Mewgenics or Slay the Spire 2 at the moment so it’s a tough time for deckbuilder recommendations, but do either of those games have vibes like this? https://youtu.be/MBWdhd9qiXw In Death Howl, you play as Ro, a hunter who has entered the ethereal spirit realm to bring back her dead son, Olvi. The spirit realm is divided into regions and once you’ve battled your way through the opening area (which also serves as the demo) you’re free to tackle the world in any order you wish. This isn’t some linear slog through various encounters; each region has its own enemies, bosses, side quests, upgrades and card sets so depending on what direction you go, your decks and playstyle will organically take on an identity of their own as you mix and match everything. The open world pretty much makes everyone’s journey through it unique which I think is incredibly cool. And while this isn’t a ‘roguelike’, this is a tough tactical game where the soulslike elements give the game some bite if you mess up, which in turn encourages you to pick your fights, prepare your deck and play carefully. You can’t just bumble through Death Howl because the only real way to restore your health and get around is by using ‘sacred groves’ which are few and far between. If you lose a fight, you can try it again as many times as you want, with the health you started it with. However, using a sacred grove to replenish your health also resets all slain enemies (similar to the Souls games’ bonfires) so self-preservation is key if you want to get anywhere. I’d often find myself in a really tight spot with low HP against some tough enemies wondering whether I should a) go back to a sacred grove to restore my health knowing that I’d have to fight my way back, hopefully returning in better shape, or… b) testing my mettle to edge out a narrow victory. One will take time, the other will take some patience, ingenuity and perhaps a bit of luck. But Death Howl feels like every part of it is working in concert. The visuals and soundscape are so evocative, so much so I’d often find myself just standing there, looking and listening (like in the video mentioned above). I can’t emphasise how good the sound effects are in this game, from the assorted, almost ASMR-like, noises you hear when collecting materials to the satisfaction of hitting ‘Continue’ on the title screen. You know those Dolby Atmos sound demos that used to be on some phones? It’s like that, but the whole game. And this extends to the music which can be menacing, melancholic and just… beautiful. These tracks remind me of some of Aphex Twin and Boards of Canada’s work: https://chrisbjorumslet.bandcamp.com/track/croaking-rot https://chrisbjorumslet.bandcamp.com/track/meadows-of-delusion Anyway, I adore Death Howl. It’s a refreshing and tremendously effective mix that’s challenging, varied and incredibly satisfying mechanically. I also really enjoyed the slowly unfolding and surprisingly affecting story. Don’t sleep on this one!

玩了一会儿，略微的不推荐。与其说是“卡牌构筑”，更像是以前游戏王在掌机上推出的作品：玩家通过交换战斗奖励获得卡牌，卡组可以随时编辑。玩法上面，有一个评论这个游戏是“魂like”，也有一点道理。游戏并非roguelike而有明确的流程，战斗中死亡只会在最近的战斗前复活。 游戏最大的问题是资源的设计，这一设计甚至影响了玩法。首先，游戏中获得新卡牌的方法是战胜怪兽掉落的资源，加上怪兽掉落的灵魂。游戏中有“篝火”，能够用杀死敌人获得的灵魂来把血量回满，并且（重点）刷新地图中已经战胜的小怪。因为小怪可以事实上无限挑战，游戏中设计的卡牌掉率比较低，平均两三局才能合成一张卡牌。另外还有一个用大量灵魂升级的技能树，能够在非常长的时间跨度上提升玩家的数值。另外，因为游戏中有能够将玩家血量方便回满的篝火，使得设计师在设计怪物数值时比较放飞自我，很多数值其实是相当夸张的。 不管游戏设计者最初的意图是什么，这一套系统实际上大大拖慢了游戏的节奏，并且很容易把玩家导向类魂游戏中最差的一类玩法：刷魂。对于玩家来说，与其直接推进游戏，挑战更新更强的boss，最舒适，甚至事后看来最节省时间的方法反而是在容易打过的几只小怪处来回战斗、坐火。直到把卡组的强度拉到一个比较高的数值。游戏的体验和游戏的手感都给人一种湿哒哒的感觉，非常不爽快。 游戏的美术非常好，无论是整体风格还是细节上的巧思。这一点是它最佳的竞争力。

Death Howl is a grid based strategy deck building game, with great paleolithic inspired art style, a touching story, and surrealist horror themes. Death Howl is a lot of things, but all elements work together to make a cohesive whole with great gameplay, atmosphere and story. Gameplay wise there are 4 areas of a large map that each contain their own unique cards that you slowly unlock while exploring and battling in those areas. As you unlock cards you will build a unique deck or two for each region. Combat itself is done on a grid and positioning is import so you need to keep in mind both what cards let you do and what your enemy is likely to do. It uses both the tactical grid and the deck building to its full extent. Combine this with archetypes that are often not immediately apparent, and there is a pretty steep learning curve. It took me a good 2 hours or more to really start to understand what to look for and what synergies to use in a deck. While this was initially frustrating, it easily became the best part of the game whenever I went into a new region and had to essentially start deckbuilding from scratch. Because of the nature of unlocking cards, being able to try combats just over and over, and starting over deck wise in new regions, I would not blame you if you compared it to a rougelike. What I don't really agree with though, is calling it a souls like. Yes you lose all "death howls" (basically souls) when you die and can try and collect them by defeating the encounter that took them... but you can spend souls anytime so if you are worried about death just spend them. Also, yes, you will need to carefully manage health as there are a number of "stone circles" (bonfires) that reset enemies but that's really just save points by another name like many games. If you are like me and hesitated to get this game because you don't like souls-like games, don't. It is nowhere near as punishing and I think the comparison is not really warranted. It needs to also be said, that the art and style of the game is great. You can see it in the trailers and on the store page, but it really combines well with the touching story but also with horrifying death imagery. Plus, it takes place in 6000BC and does a great job of having this prehistoric, shamanistic, nature vibe that is pretty unique. Lastly, I do want to make one complaint. The beginning was hard to get into because it was hard to learn the rules and get good with the game, but I can forgive that. What I do not forgive is the last boss fight changing the rules and being poorly thought out mechanics wise. The boss changed how the game fundamentally worked and didn't really explain how. I had a hunch about how it might work, and then beat the final boss of the game by playing a single card. It left a bit of a bad taste in my mouth as the final encounter of the game, but luckily the story does have a decent ending. The fact that the last boss fight was the only real complaint I had though, does mean this is a good game. Good art, good story, good gameplay. Challenging but fair, touching, grotesque, unique. I recommend this game basically to any fans of turn based games.

Death Howl has it all. 1- Solid strategy deckbuilder gameplay A turn based deckbuilder where you move on a grid is honestly not my favourite thing but this game just does it so right it made me question if I actually need to re-check the entire subgenre... or if it's just Death Howl that has clicked all the right spots for me. Cards and their effect, the environment and enemy variety just blend really well together. 2- Grind done right The game requires just a bit of grind to be enjoyed fully. I'm not talking about hours and hours, as a reference you probably just need to "completely wipe out" an area normally one time, just keep in mind that you unlock more cards the more enemies you kill and that's where the fun begins because your deck will change shape continuously and the experience will stay fresh since you play with new cards more often that not. Death Howl requires the player to adapt to every situation, not just lazily building up a deck and call it a day. 3- Beautiful pixelated world... that gives a strong feeling of isolation but also feels very much alive. It's pretty much full of events and mini-quests as well which interact with your deck and gameplay in interesting ways. 4- Simple but impactful story Just what the title says, really. It may be simple on the surface but it's narrated very thoughtfully. By the end I was captivated by it, surely something I'll remember for years. 5- Spiders Also known as the strongest enemies in the game, you may think you spaced your grid position perfectly but they will ALWAYS reach you somehow and ALWAYS poison you at some point. Deal with it.

画面非常精美，也是这款游戏最大的优点 游戏类型是战棋+卡牌+刷子+类魂 1.战棋方面：中规中矩； 2.卡牌方面：颇具特色。每个区域都有具有不同体系卡牌，分别是力量+弃牌体系、位移+背刺体系、卖血+毒药体系还有个人最喜欢的叠甲+印牌+减费体系，卡牌的机制设计挺有风格，是个加分项； 3.刷刷刷方面：肝度与挫败感的融合，较为拖累体验。卡牌需要收集材料到一定数目来解锁，而卡牌解锁后又需要打怪掉的魂+材料去合成，魂不仅要用来合卡还要拿去点技能点，（15魂一个泪滴，点一个技能需要2~3个泪滴，而每场战斗只有2~4个魂不等，直接奖励泪滴的宝箱数目稀少完全不够用）随着游戏的推进就需要去进行（并不）愉快的刷怪来保证技能点和卡牌质量跟得上，还有离谱的是在一个带有素材合成系统的游戏内，它不会告诉你缺的素材会在什么地方掉... 4.类魂方面：硬核&坐牢的叠加态。很难想象在已经有卡牌游戏不得不品的鬼抽环节的情况下，还能有小怪、精英超雄的攻击欲望与逆天的机制+主角的低性能+极其贫乏的回血手段，还有更逆天的跨区域卡牌直接加1费（基础情况下每回合5费抽5张），跨区域后旧卡组几乎瘫痪。以上因素叠加起来直接导致了游戏进程belike：打不过怪→刷刷刷升级配置→艰难蠕动过战斗→水温上升导致打不过怪→刷刷刷，好不容易过boss进了新区域发现所有区域卡加了一费导致几乎不能用于是又开始急头白脸地重复以上流程。在重复以上流程四次进入最终地图后，即便所有的卡都可以以原费用塞到一套卡组里，面对多场精英连战依旧头疼（怪物机制和技能是不写出来的，百变怪是你杀一个它可以复活一个的，诅咒牌是要卡你抽牌位的，机制是可以破甲/叠毒让你强制吃战损的） 个人认为游玩体验和它偏高的定价是不对等的，推荐那些爱好这几个标签类型和喜欢美术风格的玩家们等打折再入手

[h1]Recommended-ish[/h1] Permanent deck builders are rare, so in that space I can recommend it. However it has a very tiny pool of "neutral" cards and wants to force its area specific "intended way to play" on you very heavily. Neutral cards have normal cost in all regions, but "non-region" cards costs +1, to emphasize that you shouldn't use them. That makes the fun of building a deck and playing kind of uneven tho, depending on how you like to play and how you vibe with the area mechanics. And some enemies are so absolutely dumb to fight, I have no clue how they are in the game. There is a quite high-health enemy that just resurrects an enemy every turn, so you basically have to kill it first, but you have limited options where to start, so sometimes it's nigh impossible to get to them without being bodied by everybody on the field first. Learning what enemies can do and in what range is a bit trial and error, but it's somewhat strategic and you can try again easily and modify your deck or accessories to deal with whatever you encounter, since you spawn directly in front of an encounter, so there is little to no frustration involved.

Death Howl was an extremely beautiful experience. I loved the way it manages to incorporate the deck builder genre with grid tactics, turn-based combat and souls-like brutality. The "souls-like" needs to be taken to the letter, as it is brutal and punishing. One small mistake and back to the respawn you go. The world of the game is haunting, beautiful and extremely harsh. I loved all of the environments, the enemy design, the combat and how memorable all of the characters have been. The art and soundtrack manage to convey this otherwordly experience where I got immersed in the world of the game. The story and its presentation will stay with me for a long time. I felt and rooted for Ro, the main character, the entire time and it was such a journey to witness. Both momentous, moving and challenging. I couldn't put the game down and I have engaged very deep with it in very long play sessions. I didn't play anything else until I finished it. I am very happy to have witnessed Ro's journey and I am looking forward for the next game that this dev team will cook up.

[i][b]Revised after developer response:[/b][/i] Addicting, fantastic art, design, style, animation, sound and vfx. It feels more *visuallly* polished than it might look in it's pixel-art style. Dark Souls of card games. RnG and card complexity can be very difficult and frustrating.. and I mean PEAK FRUSTRATION. How do you play it? You die. Over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over. It's called "Death Howl" because you have to listen to your character constantly dying. Sometimes you get to watch a full-feature film of the mobs wailing on your character's entire healthbar while you do nothing but watch. I really, REALLY want to recommend this game so bad. I think it's interesting, creative, unique, *sometimes* fun, and a really great idea. However, in it's current state my opinion is this game needs serious balancing. It just isn't balanced. I keep trying to convince myself that it's just my build, or just my placement or just my decisions, but after 40 hours, I I realized.. it's just not properly tuned. Some packs have a "small red diamond" but 5 mobs with 1 of which will just infinitely respawn anything you kill. Some packs have a "large red diamond" to imply greater difficulty, but 3 easy mobs your character will destroy in 2 turns. These are all signs of just an improperly balanced game- I don't envy the dev, balancing an RNG deckbuilder with pretty strong card complexity seems like a bad time... but I cannot recommend this game in good faith until there is some major rebalancing. I'll try again in a year to see if the dev smoothed it out. Until then it's a tragic thumbs down from me. Don't say you weren't warned! Devloper, would love if you added Display Settings support, specifically for borderless fullscreen. And obviously.. please fkn balance this game. C'mon.

总算不是rogue了。它是一款以卡牌来战斗的RPG游戏，在地图上探索，击败敌人获取资源，用以制作卡牌构筑卡组。 由于每个大区域都限制其他区域的力量，所以进入新区域时，总是从一个相对低的起点开始构筑新的卡组，而每个区域都有着数个谜题或任务，通过探索和刷魂，解锁装备上限搭配各种装备，这样每个大区会有2-3种类型的卡组风格。 因为敌人组合、站位、招式固定，对此玩家需要考虑应用不同的卡组配置，甚至从更合适的方向进入战场，选择更有利的初始位置来应对，本质上本作的战斗更像是在解题，而玩家确实可以去刷满卡组再去开打。 总的来说，它的画面和缓舒适，故事简单讲诉清楚，地图探索有趣有挑战性，养成环节肝度适当，战斗风格丰富多样，成就不会错过。对我来说的唯一缺点是——完全没有画面设置……

10/10 Game, the entire experience is phenomenal. Highly recommend if you enjoy digital card games. The story is a sad but beautiful tale of loss, grief, overcoming, and acceptance. Every part of it feels natural and connected and the story follows through in a lovely linear way. Gameplay is equally stunning. After finishing the "tutorial" there are many different ways to build out decks based on your surroundings and adapt to your environment as well as different ways to utilize the quests that you are taken on. The game highly rewards you for looking around and exploring while never quite punishing you for just following the story.

Death Howl is a grid-based tactical battler that primarily uses cards to carry out attacks. That simple description doesn't capture the depth of tactical options it has. This game is a definite recommend. The game describes itself as a Souls-Like and it is extremely difficult. But, much like one of my favorite all-time games Underrail, the difficulty never feels impossible because there's always a new way to approach a fight. Throughout the game, acquiring new cards as well as other abilities and then balancing what cards you want in your deck is as important as the fights themselves. And the stamina limitations you face force you to think about each card selection and each move and attack carefully. For the gameplay alone, this game definitely makes it into my top all-time tier. The story is relatively simple; a mother is mourning the death of her son and enters the spirit-world in an effort to bring him back to life. As a parent myself, that story alone pulls at my heart strings so it's effective. I played it on my Steam Deck and you should play it on yours if you like these kind of games.
Fun deck builder, kept me entertained for the whole game with the need to build new decks in each new region. Touching story of grief.

Death Howl is a finely crafted souls-like deck builder. It features fantastic pixel art and strategic combat, as well as a heartfelt story. You will end up building multiple decks, one for each area as your cards from previous areas are no longer as viable. Building your deck while exploring and fighting bosses is the main gameplay loop, which makes the game continue to feel fresh as you go from area to area. It all just feels really well made, which is why I would recommend it strongly to anyone who is a fan of deck builders.
